name: Plum blossom
when: late January in the south, early March around Tokyo, April in Hokkaido
summary: Plum blossom comes before the cherry: a quieter, scented flower viewing.
details: Plum (ume) blooms from the far south in late January to Hokkaido in late April, a month before the cherry in each area. Dates are rough typical peaks, not a forecast; they move by a week or two each year.
price: Hotels are not yet at cherry prices.

highlights.name: Kairakuen (Mito)
highlights.note: About 3,000 trees in one of the three great gardens.

highlights.name: Atami Plum Garden
highlights.note: Early-blooming; also holds the Atami Baien Plum Festival.

name: Hydrangea
when: early June in Kyushu, mid to late June around Tokyo, July in Tohoku and Hokkaido
summary: Hydrangea (ajisai) peaks in the rainy season, so the temples are best on a wet day.
details: Hydrangea (ajisai) blooms with the plum rain (tsuyu), moving north from early June. Dates are rough typical peaks, not a forecast; they move by a week or two each year.

highlights.name: Meigetsu-in (Kamakura)
highlights.note: The "hydrangea temple" with its blue hydrangeas.

highlights.name: Hakone Tozan Railway
highlights.note: A train through illuminated hydrangeas in the evening.

name: Red spider lily (higanbana)
when: late September, a little later further north
summary: Fields of red spider lilies (higanbana, the "flower of the other shore") bloom for a short week around the autumn equinox.
details: Higanbana (spider lily), also called flower of the dead or hell flower in Japan, blooms around the autumn equinox (Higan) when the family graves are visited. It flowers for about a week and is gone by October. Dates are rough typical peaks, not a forecast; they move by a week or two each year.
crowd: Fields are busiest on the weekends of the peak week.

highlights.name: Kinchakuda (Hidaka)
highlights.note: About five million lilies in one park; the best known site.

highlights.name: Gonkitsune no Sato (Handa)
highlights.note: The lilies by Niimi Nankichi's fox story.

highlights.name: Inabuchi terraces (Asuka)
highlights.note: Lilies framing rice terraces among old burial mounds.

name: Cosmos
when: September in Hokkaido, October in the north and central Honshu, early November in the south
summary: Fields of cosmos flowers in autumn, with the red kochia at the same time in Hitachi Seaside Park.
details: Cosmos (kosumosu, "autumn cherry") covers hill and field slopes in autumn, earliest in Hokkaido. Dates are rough typical peaks, not a forecast; they move by a week or two each year.

highlights.name: Hitachi Seaside Park
highlights.note: Cosmos and the red kochia bushes.

name: Nemophila (baby blue eyes)
when: late April to early May, Hitachinaka
summary: A hill of about five million pale blue nemophila flowers in Hitachi Seaside Park.
crowd: Heavy weekend crowds and traffic in Golden Week.

name: Wisteria
when: late April to mid May
summary: Hanging wisteria (fuji) tunnels and trellises, most famous at Ashikaga Flower Park.
details: Wisteria blooms from late April; the great sites hold light-ups at night. Dates are rough typical peaks, not a forecast; they move by a week or two each year.

name: Moss phlox (shibazakura)
when: late April in Chichibu, early May at Fuji, late May in Hokkaido
summary: Carpets of pink moss phlox, a "ground cherry" bloom that follows the sakura.
details: Moss phlox (shibazakura) carpets open from late April on the Kanto hills, with Fuji at the start of May and Hokkaido at the end of May. Dates are rough typical peaks, not a forecast; they move by a week or two each year.

name: Lavender (Furano)
when: early to late July, Furano and Biei
summary: Purple fields of lavender at Farm Tomita and the Biei hills.
details: Lavender at Furano blooms for about two weeks around mid July; Biei flowers run on to September. Dates are rough typical peaks, not a forecast; they move by a week or two each year.
crowd: Busy on weekends; the best fields are best in the morning.

highlights.name: Farm Tomita (Furano)
highlights.note: Lavender fields, with the other flower stripes.

highlights.name: Shikisai no Oka (Biei)
highlights.note: Rolling hills of flower stripes through the summer.

name: Sunflowers (Hokuryu)
when: early to mid August, Hokuryu, Hokkaido
summary: Hokkaido sunflower field with about 1.5 million plants, the largest in Japan.

highlights.name: Akeno Sunflower Festival (Hokuto)
highlights.note: About 600,000 sunflowers with the Southern Alps behind.

name: Fireflies (hotaru)
when: late May to mid June, Moriyama, Shiga
summary: Genji fireflies in the Moriyama river valleys in June, among the best known in Japan.

name: Snow monsters (juhyo, Zao)
when: late January to late February, Zao, Yamagata
summary: Trees coated in rime and snow into giant ghost shapes on the Zao ski slopes.
details: The Zao ropeway runs over the forest; floodlights light the monsters up on some evenings.

name: Drift ice (Abashiri)
when: late January to mid March, Abashiri, Hokkaido
summary: Sea ice floating on the Okhotsk Sea, viewed from icebreaker tours.
crowd: Tours are timed to when the ice arrives; check the day before.

name: Humpback whales (Okinawa)
when: January to March, Kerama Islands, Naha
summary: Humpbacks come to the warm waters around Okinawa to breed.
aliases: ホエールウォッチング

highlights.name: Kerama Islands
highlights.note: Whale-watching boats from Naha, Zamami and Tokashiki.

name: Kawazu cherry blossom
when: February to early March, Kawazu, Izu
summary: The early pink cherry that blooms in February along the Kawazu river, with a month-long festival.
crowd: Busy weekends; trains from Tokyo are the easy way.

name: Rice paddy art (Inakadate)
when: July to September, Inakadate, Aomori
summary: Paddies planted with several colors of rice to form giant pictures.

name: Pampas grass (Sengokuhara)
when: mid October to early November, Hakone
summary: The Sengokuhara pampas grass field, golden at sunset.

name: Kobe Luminarie
when: early December, Kobe
summary: Light arches built in memory of the 1995 earthquake.
crowd: Queues of an hour or more; one-way crowd control.

name: Nabana no Sato Winter Illumination
when: mid October to early May, Nagashima, Mie
summary: One of Japan's biggest light-ups.

name: Ashikaga Flower Fantasy
when: late October to mid February, Ashikaga
summary: The wisteria garden turned into a night park of about five million lights.
aliases: あしかがフラワーパーク

name: Shirakawa-go Winter Light-up
when: a few evenings in late January and February, Shirakawa-go
summary: Thatched farmhouses lit up in the snow on selected evenings.
